sentences.text: Asos has told its customers that hackers are in possession of detailed profiles of potentially millions of the online store's users.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: It issued the update after BBC News told the retailer it had been contacted by cyber criminals who said this week's breach went beyond the "basic contact details" Asos previously said might have been accessed.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: Names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, customer numbers and dates of birth are now in the hands of criminals.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: One victim told the BBC it was "very unsettling" that the hackers now know these things about her.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: The criminals also have access to the searches customers have made on the website.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: Terms like "reclaimed vintage", "glamorous wide fit" and "Asos petite" are visible in the data.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: Harriet has been using Asos since 2019 - another detail the hackers now know.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: "What I find particularly worrying is the possibility that stolen data can be used as a tool for for future attacks, meaning the impact of a breach could extend well beyond the initial incident," she said.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: With the stolen information, scammers may be able to create convincing phishing attack emails or phone calls.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: The risk to individuals is now higher and customers are being warned about potential impersonation scams.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: In its email to customers, Asos confirmed data profiles were taken but said no bank details or passwords were accessed.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: "Please remain cautious of unexpected messages or calls claiming to be from Asos," it said.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: "We will never ask you to share passwords, security codes or payment details through an unsolicited message or call." The company did not respond to questions about the scale of the breach.

sentences.text: Customers saw this pop up notification on Tuesday The high profile hack made global headlines on Tuesday when cyber criminals used Asos's own app system to send a pop up notification to potentially millions of people.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: Later that day the firm confirmed to shareholders via the London Stock Exchange that the pop up was sent by an "unauthorised third party" and "basic personal information including name and contact details may have been accessed." The company then sent an email to customers with similar wording.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: On Wednesday evening the cyber criminals responsible contacted the BBC sharing a sample of the stolen data which showed the true extent of the hack.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: The BBC held off publishing this article to allow Asos to contact its customers first.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: Asos said it is still investigating the data breach and it would "contact customers directly where we believe additional information, support or action may be required".
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: The UK fashion site explained to customers that hackers gained access to an Asos employee account by "impersonating a trusted contact to obtain log in credentials".
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: With that log in to an unnamed service, the hackers were able to download the customer data.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: In the pop up notification send to customers by the hackers, they claimed they had "compromised the Snowflake instance".
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: Snowflake is a popular data storage and analysis company whose customers have been breached in the past due to unauthorised log ins.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: The cyber criminals, calling themselves Xuanyewen, claimed to the BBC they used a platform which is built natively on top of Snowflake - called Simon AI - to gain access to the data.

sentences.text: Simon AI has been contacted for comment.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: Snowflake previously said its platform had not been breached.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: Asos said customers are not being asked to take any action.
sentences.article_title: Asos hackers took more personal details than first revealed, BBC finds

sentences.text: But cyber security experts have warned users to change passwords as a precaution and be on alert for suspicious activity.

sentences.text: "Passwords have not been stolen, so be highly suspicious of any unsolicited text or email asking you to change or share yours," said Trevor Dearing, Senior Director of Critical Infrastructure at Illumio.

sentences.text: "Expect scammers to mention the attack, use your personal details to seem genuine, and create urgency, such as threatening to lock your account within 24 hours." Asos said its website and app are safe to use and "we know our customers trust us with their information".

sentences.text: Mia St Hilaire died after drinking a milkshake in August 2023 The family of a 12-year-old girl who died after drinking a milkshake made in an unwashed blender at a cafe have called for a dedicated rating that scores food businesses on their allergy management.
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: Mia St Hilaire, who had a tree nut allergy, suffered an anaphylactic shock and died after she drank a Twix milkshake at the Pop Inn Cafe in Bermondsey, south-east London, in August 2023.
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: Her order contained hazelnut residue because the blender had not been washed after a Kinder Bueno milkshake was made in it beforehand, an inquest concluded on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: In a statement, her family said "significant changes" were needed to protect people with food allergies.
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: In January 2025, the cafe was fined £18,000 and its proprietor Baris Yucel was given 100 hours of community service after admitting six criminal charges related to the Food Safety Act.
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: These included not making allergen advice available or visible to consumers, failing to manage allergen contamination during the food production process, and serving food that contained an allergenic ingredient that was not supposed to be present.
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: CCTV evidence showed that Yucel had not cleaned the blender before preparing Mia's milkshake.
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: Mia's parents said their "deeply loved" daughter would never be forgotten Assistant coroner Briony Ballard listened to evidence at London Inner South Coroner's Court before publishing a narrative conclusion on Mia's death.
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: In a statement read after the conclusion of the inquest, Mia's parents Adrian St Hilaire and Chanel Spence said families with food allergies should not be "at risk" when eating out.
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: "We hope that lessons will be learned from Mia's death and that changes will be made to prevent other families enduring the devastation that we now have to live with," they said.
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: "Consumers rely on food hygiene ratings when deciding where it is safe to eat, but they do not tell us anything about the way a food business runs allergy management systems.
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: "There should be a separate, clearly displayed rating dedicated to the allergy management, like the food hygiene rating.
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: "This would mean that people with allergies could make more informed choices about where they eat." Natasha's Foundation founder Tanya Ednan-Laperouse, whose daughter died aged 15 from an allergy to sesame in a Pret A Manger baguette, said allergies were "a serious, unpredictable medical condition".
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: "The inquest into Mia's death illustrates just how far we still have to go to improve awareness, understanding and regulation of food allergies," she said.
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: "Food businesses must take allergen risks seriously, every time," she said.
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: "People have the right to know exactly what is in their food and drink, and it is a business's legal duty to provide accurate allergen information.
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: "We recently produced new guidance for businesses to make sure they understand their responsibilities to inform consumers about allergens, including the risk of cross-contact, and we are keeping this policy under review.
sentences.article_title: Death of 12-year-old girl prompts call for allergy management ratings

sentences.text: We also have free allergy training and practical tools that businesses can use." Listen to the best of BBC Radio London on Sounds and follow BBC London on Facebook , external , X , external and Instagram , external .

sentences.text: Jo Farrell said she expected more accusations of violence towards women by serving police officers would come to light Police Scotland has said 45 serving officers are currently suspended over allegations of violence against women and girls.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: Chief constable Jo Farrell said she expected more would face sanctions over their behaviour following a spate of former officers being convicted for sexual offences.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: Farrell said a review into the handling of the case surrounding officer Alan Greer – who was exposed as a serial rapist after taking his own life – was under way.

sentences.text: She added about 8,000 members of staff were still to be "re-vetted" for their roles after a change in regulations earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: First minister John Swinney said he had "full confidence" in Police Scotland and the renewed vetting process.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: In an interview with BBC Scotland News, Farrell described the scale of violence against women and girls in Scotland as an "epidemic", and that police forces were not immune to the problem.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: She said: "We've got in the order of between currently 40 and 50 people currently suspended, so not at work, who are being investigated for offences that relate to violence against women and girls.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: "Those investigations are at various stages." This video can not be played Farrell said women should be confident to come forward and report offending by police officers Police Scotland later clarified 45 officers were under suspension over allegations of violence against women and girls.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: Not all are currently part of a criminal investigation, the force said.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: A BBC Disclosure investigation in July revealed that Greer had repeatedly attacked and attempted to murder women over a 14-year period.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: Further inquiries uncovered that Greer had passed vetting checks to join what was then Strathclyde Police in 2009, despite having two reports of criminal behaviour against women on his record.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: Greer took his own life in May at the age of 47.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: "It is an ongoing investigation, but it is also subject to an independent review to find out whether there were any opportunities to identify his offending earlier and whether there is any learning from that," she told BBC Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: "What is important is that we get that independent review, that colleagues elsewhere in the United Kingdom are looking at that case to identify whether there were any opportunities that were missed." Greer is one of three former officers in Scotland to be exposed as rapists this year.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: In July, Cameron Ross was jailed for 10 years after he was found guilty of raping two women and threatening to kill another in Stornoway, on the Isle of Lewis, and in Inverness over a 10-year period.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: Ross, 39, has since launched an appeal against both his conviction and his sentence.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: Last month, former police sergeant Campbell Petrie , 50, was found guilty of a series of sex attacks on women between 2006 and 2023.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: Petrie - who was first arrested following a complaint by one of his victims 17 years ago – was convicted of two counts of rape and a number of other charges including physical and sexual abuse towards two women in Glasgow.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: He was suspended by Police Scotland after being charged with the offences in December 2023 but retired from the force two years later.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: Another officer, Jay Skivington, 24, was sentenced in October to 160 hours of unpaid work and given five-year non-harassment order for violent offences against a woman .
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: About 8,000 Police Scotland staff, including 6,000 officers, are due to be re-vetted after procedures were tightened Farrell said that between 300 and 400 officers had now been re-vetted as part of new rules brought in following the murder of Sarah Everard by Met Police officer Wayne Couzens .
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: About 6,000 officers and 2,000 civilian staff still have to go through the new vetting process.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: She said the rules would make it easier to "exit people" found to be unsuitable to serve in the force.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: "It's only now during this year there has been a change in the vetting regime.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: So for the first time, if an officer fails their vetting, they can be exited from policing," she said.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: "So that is a very recent change, and a welcome change from my point of view.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: He said: "We've done work over the last number of years on vetting and police conduct on a number of areas that have highlighted where Police Scotland can improve and they are making improvements in those areas.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: He said he did not believe there was a cultural problem in the ranks of Police Scotland and said there was a wider societal issue with violence against women.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: He added vetting of potential police recruits needed to be stronger and called for more funding for the system to allow current vetting to include home visits, deeper reference interviews and psychometric testing.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: Kennedy said: "You're always worried about reputation as a police officer.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: When Wayne Couzens was identified the reputation of police across the UK was horrendous.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: "But that is just a very small part of policing.
sentences.article_title: Forty five Scottish police officers suspended over alleged crimes against women, says chief constable

sentences.text: The public should feel trusting and safe with police officers." David Kennedy said he did not believe Police Scotland had a "cultural problem" with violence against women but it was part of a wider societal issue Swinney said he had made tackling violence against women and girls a "fundamental priority".

sentences.text: Thames Valley Police has accepted warrants it used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes at the time of his arrest in February were unlawful, the High Court was told.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: Following Thursday's hearing, items seized in the raid continue to be held by the police, with a further hearing to take place in 2027 to decide whether the material can be used as evidence.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the criminal investigation into Mountbatten-Windsor is continuing.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: The former prince, who denies any wrongdoing, was arrested by police on 19 February on suspicion of misconduct in public office, after which he launched a legal challenge over the legality of the search warrants.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: The force said it accepted that the "initial court's decision to issue warrants under the specific piece of legislation used was incorrect" before they searched the properties.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: On Thursday at the High Court, Judge Mr Justice Hilliard said Mountbatten-Windsor and the police had agreed that the search warrants had been unlawful.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: However, he added: "The fact that the search warrants were quashed does not bring the investigation to an end or mean that the whole of the investigation is unlawful." Mountbatten-Windsor opposes the police's bid to retain the evidence, the judge said, and another hearing is expected in 2027.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: Mountbatten-Windsor remains under police investigation despite a ruling that the way search warrants were issued was unlawful His lawyers have used a judicial review to challenge the actions of the force's chief constable and the Central Criminal Court in the build-up to his arrest.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: His arrest arose after the US Department of Justice published documents which raised suspicions he had forwarded confidential information to the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein when Mountbatten-Windsor was a UK trade envoy in 2010.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: He has consistently denied any wrongdoing in relation to Epstein.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: The court heard on Thursday that Thames Valley Police seized documents and electronic devices when they raided Mountbatten-Windsor's homes earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: Thames Valley Police's position was that they had applied for search warrants under section eight and nine of the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 at a hearing at the Central Criminal Court the day before the search.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: That court determined that only section eight search warrants were needed and they were granted on that basis - but subsequently, a legal challenge has established that the court should have issued them under the section nine.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: The judge explained on Thursday why the police could keep hold of the former prince's items that had been seized.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: "We ensured the court was presented with all the necessary information and paperwork to inform their decision, following the correct legal processes throughout.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: "We accept the position that the initial court's decision to issue warrants under the specific piece of legislation used was incorrect and therefore these must be legally quashed.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: The next stage in this legal dispute will be a behind-closed-doors hearing over whether the police can still retain material seized from Mountbatten-Windsor's homes under alternative powers designed for situations like this.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: The error that has led to Thames Valley Police accepting the search warrants were unlawful relates to the particular power the judge permitted the force to use when its officers raided the properties.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: Strict legal safeguards on searches bar the police from automatically seizing sensitive material without thinking through in advance the need to take it.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: Examples of that material include advice from a suspect's lawyer or material which does not really belong to them, such as copies of confidential work-related papers from an employer.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: In practice, if the police find such material during a search, they should return it rather than use it in their investigation.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: The category of search warrant that was granted by the court in this instance did not take into account the possibility of such protected material being seized.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: However, the law says police can in fact seize that kind of material - or potentially retain it in the event of an error - providing they pass some extra tests.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: Thames Valley Police must now convince a judge that the material is likely to be of "substantial value" to their investigation into Mountbatten-Windsor and, ultimately, potential evidence to present to a court.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: So while the force has conceded the search warrant was unlawful, a judge will have to decide whether this alternative search power, with its extra safeguards, justifies them keeping and using the material after all.
sentences.article_title: Warrants used to search Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful, court says

sentences.text: Young appeared in court on Thursday wearing a grey police-issue sweatshirt and spoke to confirm his personal details A junior Royal Navy sailor accused of preparing to spy for Russia has appeared in court.
sentences.article_title: Royal Navy sailor in court accused of preparing to spy for Russia

sentences.text: Able Seaman Teddy Young, who specialised in warfare intelligence, allegedly retained UK defence and intelligence material that he had access to and made preparations to disclose sensitive information, a court was told.
sentences.article_title: Royal Navy sailor in court accused of preparing to spy for Russia

sentences.text: The 24-year-old appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday after being charged under the National Security Act.
sentences.article_title: Royal Navy sailor in court accused of preparing to spy for Russia

sentences.text: The BBC understands that the allegations against Young include translating a message into Russian and looking for a web portal that invited people to submit information to Russia.
sentences.article_title: Royal Navy sailor in court accused of preparing to spy for Russia

sentences.text: Wearing a police-issue grey sweatshirt, Young spoke in court to confirm his name, date of birth and his address in Clapham, near Bedford.
sentences.article_title: Royal Navy sailor in court accused of preparing to spy for Russia

sentences.text: He is formally charged with engaging in conduct in preparation for disclosing protected information, and obtaining, copying, recording or retaining protected information, intending the conduct to benefit a foreign power.
sentences.article_title: Royal Navy sailor in court accused of preparing to spy for Russia

sentences.text: The charges cover a period between 26 November 2024 and 21 May 2025.
sentences.article_title: Royal Navy sailor in court accused of preparing to spy for Russia

sentences.text: Police said the alleged offences were not related to the recent RAF Fairford incident that resulted in a number of arrests after suspicious activity was reported near the base.
sentences.article_title: Royal Navy sailor in court accused of preparing to spy for Russia

sentences.text: In total, seven men have been arrested and later released on bail in connection with the incident, which is being investigated by counter-terror police.
sentences.article_title: Royal Navy sailor in court accused of preparing to spy for Russia

sentences.text: Young was arrested at his home address in Bedfordshire on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Royal Navy sailor in court accused of preparing to spy for Russia

sentences.text: He is the first member of the armed forces to be charged under the new National Security Act 2023.
sentences.article_title: Royal Navy sailor in court accused of preparing to spy for Russia

sentences.text: Cdr Helen Flanagan, head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, said: "These are very serious charges against a serving member of the armed forces.
sentences.article_title: Royal Navy sailor in court accused of preparing to spy for Russia

sentences.text: He will next appear at the Old Bailey on 16 October.

sentences.text: Jane Adetoro, 36, Christina Walters, 32, and Rebecca Walters, 31, had been living "very secluded lives" following the death of their mother, who drowned in 2010, senior coroner Penelope Schofield said.

sentences.text: On 11 May, the women - who had all been living together in Greenford, London - visited an area of Birmingham close to where their mother died before travelling the next day to Brighton beach, where they drowned in adverse sea conditions in the early hours of 13 May.

sentences.text: The coroner said they could not swim.

sentences.article_title: Three sisters who drowned in sea off Brighton took own lives, inquest finds

sentences.text: In an emotional statement read out on his behalf, he said he watched his daughters grow from little girls to beautiful, intelligent women "with a special place in my heart".

sentences.article_title: Three sisters who drowned in sea off Brighton took own lives, inquest finds

sentences.text: "To lose all three of my precious daughters is a heartbreak beyond anything I could ever have imagined." He could not understand why his daughters' lives ended so suddenly, and hoped they were reunited with their mother "in God's eternal care", he added.

sentences.text: Shaun of the Dead and Mission: Impossible films star Simon Pegg has revealed he has been diagnosed with ADHD, which he said "confirmed a lot of stuff that I'd been wrestling with".
sentences.article_title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'

sentences.text: Pegg, 56, who also co-created and starred in films Hot Fuzz, The World's End, and TV series Spaced, said "there was a lot of build-up and suspicion, and it just took a while actually to get there." Speaking on the podcast I'm ADHD!
sentences.article_title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'

sentences.text: No You're Not , external on Thursday, he said he pursued a diagnosis as he "just wanted to know".
sentences.article_title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'

sentences.text: ADHD symptoms focus on three main areas - inattention, hyperactivity and impulsivity plus lack of concentration.
sentences.article_title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'

sentences.text: Although many people may feel like they have some similar symptoms, genetics play an important role in ADHD and a full diagnosis is given to those who are negatively affected on a daily basis.
sentences.article_title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'

sentences.text: Pegg said he had previously been putting his symptoms down to "just character fault".
sentences.article_title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'

sentences.text: The actor and writer also spoke about his mental health, including having clinical depression and struggling to control his drinking, which he said he initially thought had "caused" his diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'

sentences.text: "I felt like it was something that had come on in later life because I wasn't a naughty child.
sentences.article_title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'

sentences.text: "I've had bouts of depression in my adult life since 18 and I thought maybe it had come on with that.
sentences.article_title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'

sentences.text: "Maybe over the years with therapy and medication - whatever - I've been treating the symptoms and not the cause of why I feel that way." Pegg said: "I did feel different in a way I might not be able to put my finger on.
sentences.article_title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'

sentences.text: Maybe everybody feels that way.
sentences.article_title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'

sentences.text: "I just assumed ADHD kids were kind of chaotic and difficult and didn't pay attention in school," he added.
sentences.article_title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'

sentences.text: "But there were other things that I did do as a kid – fidget or whatever – that made me think, 'Oh no, maybe I've had this longer than I thought'." Pegg said his wife has been supportive and is "dealing with it as if I'd been diagnosed ages ago", adding: "It's just who I am, and it's just things that I do.
sentences.article_title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'

sentences.text: "She makes allowances for forgetfulness and and lack of concentration." ADHD has rewired the workplace.
sentences.article_title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'

sentences.text: "And it's because of a lack of focus and ability to kind of totally focus.

sentences.text: ADHD is described by the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (Nice) as "a behavioural syndrome characterised by hyperactivity, impulsivity, and inattention".
sentences.article_title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'

sentences.article_title: Actor Simon Pegg reveals ADHD diagnosis: 'It's just who I am'

sentences.text: The NHS in England experienced its busiest September on record There are "ominous signs" that winter pressures are already affecting the NHS in England, according to senior health leaders.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: The warning comes as new data reveals the waiting list for routine hospital treatment in England rose for the second month in a row.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: An estimated 7.37 million treatments were waiting to be carried out at the end of August, relating to 6.24 million patients.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: The numbers are the highest since October 2025 and have raised questions over whether the NHS will meet a government target of treating 92% of patients within 18 weeks by 2029.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: The rise in waiting lists comes despite the NHS in England delivering what were described as record levels of planned, elective care over the summer, while demand for services also reached its highest level ever.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: A record 4.7 million planned treatments, procedures and appointments occurred across June, July and August – more than in any previous summer.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: But both A&Es and ambulance services also saw a record number of patients for the month of September.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: NHS England's national medical director, Professor Frankie Swords, warned that despite the progress delivered by frontline teams, winter pressure was already building.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: "Staff are already seeing the ominous early signs of pressure, with more patients coming to A&E with flu and other respiratory viruses than usual for this time of year, and unfortunately many people are still waiting longer than we would like them to," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: The NHS Alliance, which represents hospitals, says the government in England is not going to achieve its manifesto promise of hitting the 18-week hospital waiting time target by the end of the parliament in 2029.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: That 18-week target hasn't been hit for a decade.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: A separate analysis by the Health Foundation think-tank said progress on cutting waiting times had stalled over the past year, with referrals on to the waiting list rising at a much quicker rate than the number of patients being treated.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: More patients, including children, have been arriving at A&E departments with flu and other respiratory viruses.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: The number of patients seen within four hours in A&Es last month fell to 74.4%,  down from 75.0% in August.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: The number of people waiting more than 12 hours in A&E departments from a decision to admit to actually being admitted – what is known as "corridor care" – stood at 50,582 in September, up from 44,951 in August.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: That has alarmed Dr Vicky Price, president of the Society for Acute Medicine.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: "A 13% year-on-year rise in 12-hour emergency department waits as winter approaches should set alarm bells ringing.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: "More than 50,000 patients waited over 12 hours from the decision to admit to admission in September - 1,686 people every day.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: "These are not just numbers.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: "They represent vulnerable people who are waiting far too long for a bed and staff trying to deliver safe care in overcrowded emergency departments." The government says the 18-week mark could still be achieved, saying it was investing in NHS buildings and equipment to make services more productive.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: It also pointed to disruption to care that was caused by the strikes by resident doctors, a dispute which has now been settled.
sentences.article_title: 'Ominous signs' of winter pressures as NHS waiting list grows

sentences.text: But the strain that services are feeling in September, before winter has even really got going, will be a cause for concern among NHS leaders and their political bosses alike.

sentences.text: Airport chiefs said plans would create more than 50,000 jobs, including 3,800 on site Birmingham Airport has announced a £2bn expansion plan which bosses say could more than double passenger numbers and create thousands of jobs.

sentences.article_title: Birmingham Airport announces £2bn expansion

sentences.text: The fresh charges against the couple were made public on Thursday and are in addition to the drug-trafficking and weapons charges already brought against them, which they have denied.
sentences.article_title: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture

sentences.text: Maduro, 63, and Flores, 69, have been in custody since January in a detention centre in Brooklyn, where they were taken after US forces seized them in a pre-dawn raid on their compound in the Venezuelan capital, Caracas.

sentences.text: Barry J Pollack, Maduro's attorney, said his client denies the new charges and looks forward to his day in court.

sentences.text: Federal prosecutors also announced on Thursday that Flores was added to the earlier narco-terrorism charge.
sentences.article_title: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture

sentences.text: The trial for both Maduro and Flores is set to begin in June 2027.
sentences.article_title: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture

sentences.text: Both are being held in a detention centre in Brooklyn and are expected to remain there after Flores's request to be moved to house arrest was denied by a judge on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture

sentences.text: The new accusations relate to the alleged torture of US citizens who were being held in Venezuela while Maduro was in power.
sentences.article_title: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture

sentences.text: The superseding indictment unsealed on Thursday accuses the former presidential couple of "entrenching themselves in power" by presiding "over a system of repression that relied on violence against political opposition, arbitrary detention, and the torture of detainees, including United States citizens".

sentences.text: According to the indictment, the torture included "electric shock, asphyxiation, rape, forced nudity, prolonged isolation, starvation, punishment cells, and psychological torture".
sentences.article_title: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture

sentences.text: The prosecutors allege that the psychological torture included threats to kill victims' families, including children.
sentences.article_title: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture

sentences.text: "All of this was done to ensure that  Maduro and Flores retained their power," prosecutors said outside the courthouse on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture

sentences.text: "This conduct, we allege, has caused significant harm to Americans, to US citizens", prosecutors said, calling it "the epitome of corruption".
sentences.article_title: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture

sentences.text: The request by Cilia Flores for house arrest was denied The prosecution accuses Flores of having played a key role in the development of the repressive system, ordering that individuals be tortured and even receiving updates on the torture of specific prisoners.

sentences.text: Faisal Shoukat, pictured leaving court, previously sat on Calderdale Council A former councillor has been found guilty of running a bogus coronavirus testing laboratory during the Covid-19 pandemic.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: Faisal Shoukat, who served on Calderdale Council, was convicted of causing public nuisance, fraudulent trading and money laundering after a trial at Bradford Crown Court.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: Four other people on trial alongside Shoukat -  former justice minister Shahid Malik, Lynn Connell, Paul Moore and Dr Alexander Zarneh - were cleared of any wrongdoing.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: The verdicts were returned by His Honour Judge Chris Smith after the jury was discharged in April during their deliberations, when one member of the panel was arrested on suspicion of conspiring to pervert the course of justice.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: Judge Smith criticised a catalogue of "systemic failures" at the business, for which Shoukat was responsible for the day-to-day running, telling the court: "The overriding thought at the time was simply to make money.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: "Put simply, profit was put before professionalism and public safety." RT Diagnostics was set up in March 2021 with Shoukat and Mr Malik named among the directors, after the government invited private companies to help meet the demand for testing, including so-called 'Fit-to-Fly' tests.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: Prosecutors said 39-year-old Shoukat - who was a Labour councillor at the time - was the "controlling mind" of the Halifax-based firm.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: However, the court heard that test kits sent out to customers - sourced from Turkey - did not meet the required standards in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: It was also said the lab had returned a "suspiciously low" number of positive tests .
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: Between May and July 2021 it reported 138,738 tests, but only 45 of these were positive, with 123,058 showing as negative and one indeterminate.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: A video published by The Sun newspaper in July of that year alleged tests were being dumped in a side room.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: The video also showed the firm's laboratory at Park Works to be in poor condition, with rubbish strewn across the floor, its ceiling exposed and bin bags dumped outside.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: Medical safety inspectors described the site on Lister Lane as a "building site" and said there was evidence of people living there.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: Delivering his verdicts, Judge Smith criticised the company's "cavalier" and "careless" approach to the accreditation process, which would allow it to conduct testing.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: There were also "systemic failures" with the company and the service it provided, he added.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: Customers experienced a "multitude of problems", the judge said, from test kits being delivered in unsealed boxes to results not being issued.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: Describing the testing and reporting systems at RT Diagnostics as "profoundly flawed", he said there was also evidence some samples "had simply not been tested".
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: One customer was told he and his wife had tested positive for the virus, only to later receive an email from RT Diagnostics which said they had tested negative.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: Despite the firm only trading for a two-month period, almost 80% of the 1,218 Trustpilot reviews it received were one star.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: Mr Malik, who cried after he was cleared of wrongdoing, was also paid a similar amount as a co-director, the court heard.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: He was not involved in the day-to-day running of the company, and lived outside of the UK for part of its short-lived tenure.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: Mr Malik, 58, of Colne Rd, Burnley, was found not guilty of causing a public nuisance, fraudulent trading and money laundering.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: Ms Connell, 65, of Wagon Farm, Ripponden, Mr Moore, 57, of Plober Street, Burnley, and Dr Zarneh, 71, of Wood Lane, Halifax, were all found not guilty of causing a public nuisance and fraudulent trading.
sentences.article_title: Ex-councillor guilty of running sham Covid-19 lab

sentences.text: A photo taken from within a classroom showed an armed police officer at the scene A schoolgirl who was stabbed by a masked fellow pupil at school described how she told a teacher "Sir, I've been stabbed" after the attack.
sentences.article_title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed'

sentences.text: Police were called to Thorpe St Andrew School, near Norwich, on 11 March, following reports that a 15-year-old girl had been stabbed in the back.
sentences.article_title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed'

sentences.text: The defendant, who is now 16 and cannot be named for legal reasons, has denied a charge of attempted murder, but has admitted possessing a kitchen knife without lawful authority and wounding with intent.

sentences.text: In a police interview played to the jury at King's Lynn Crown Court, the girl said she had been in "panic mode" and felt numb and weak.
sentences.article_title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed'

sentences.text: Describing the attack, which took place in a corridor, she said she had seen a masked person dressed "head to toe in black, no school uniform whatsoever".
sentences.article_title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed'

sentences.text: The boy did not say anything to her and she did not recognise him, she added.
sentences.article_title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed'

sentences.text: She said she turned away and it "felt like he touched me on the shoulder, then it felt like he punched me".
sentences.article_title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed'

sentences.text: She said she "didn't know I was stabbed at this point" but after turning into a classroom, "I went 'Sir, I've been stabbed.'" The girl said the school lockdown bell sounded and staff gave first aid.
sentences.article_title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed'

sentences.text: Of the incident itself, she said that once she had opened the door, "I felt sharp pain shooting through my back, I went like that and it was blood all over my hands".
sentences.article_title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed'

sentences.text: She said in the interview, carried out days after the incident: "I don't think it's hit me properly yet.
sentences.article_title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed'

sentences.text: "It's just a bit of a shock." Police were called to Thorpe St Andrew School at 10:24 GMT on 11 March Stephen Rose KC, for the defence, asked the girl, who gave evidence in court, whether she had had any issues with the boy.

sentences.text: She wiped tears from her eyes and asked for a break during her evidence.
sentences.article_title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed'

sentences.text: Another female pupil at the school, who witnessed the attack, said in a video-recorded police interview that the boy "came up behind [the girl] and just stabbed her in the back near her shoulder".
sentences.article_title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed'

sentences.article_title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed'

sentences.text: Asked at what point she had first seen the knife, she said: "As he raised it." The trial at King's Lynn Crown Court is expected to last three weeks The court has already been told that the defendant had written notes saying he hated women .

sentences.article_title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed'

sentences.text: To all readers out there in the UK and perhaps even the world.
sentences.article_title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed'

sentences.text: If you're reading this, I am either dead or in custody.
sentences.article_title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed'

sentences.text: "I imagine the police will be the first to read this and seize it as evidence, so I will make something very clear.
sentences.article_title: Schoolgirl told teacher 'Sir, I've been stabbed'

sentences.text: I made this decision to do so on my own." Another note read: "Am I evil for that?

sentences.text: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning Like "being shot out of a cannon" is the closest comparison that driver Susanne Callin can come up with for the extreme motorsport she competes in.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: She is a two-time European champion in Top Fuel drag racing - often described as the fastest sport on the planet.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Races begin with a bone-shaking roar, as the world's fastest-accelerating cars leave the starting line, flames bursting out of their exhaust pipes.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: The cars surge to more than 300mph (483km/h) in races that last just four seconds, with drivers experiencing more g-force than an astronaut launching into space.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: It is the only elite class of motorsport where women frequently beat men to major titles.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Women have won seven out of the past nine European Championships, while, until recently, female US driver Brittany Force held the world speed record in the sport.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: In comparison, it is 50 years since a woman even competed in a Formula 1 Grand Prix race.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Women account for about 10% of participants across motorsport, and just 4% of elite drivers, according to campaign group More Than Equal.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: However, they made up 20% of the drivers competing in this year's US and European Top Fuel seasons.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: So why is this high-velocity motorsport bucking the trend?
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Top Fuel drivers experience more g-force than an astronaut launching into space More Than Equal has described drag racing as "the most gender-equal motorsport in the world".
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Top Fuel is its most extreme form, named in reference to the powerful nitromethane fuel the cars run on.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Races take place on a straight track, just 1,000 feet (305 metres) long.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Usually, two cars race each other.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: The intense g-force hits in the first second of the race, as the cars go from stationary to 100mph, with a second gut punch following as the clutch fully engages about half-way through.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: The adrenalin rush is "extremely addictive", Swedish driver Callin, aged 43, tells BBC Global Women.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Concern over the risks "is always there" she says, but "the safety really does work".
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Drivers are highly protected and safety precautions have been boosted further after fatal crashes in nitromethane-fuelled cars in 2004 and 2008, with races reduced in length.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Callin says she has never felt underestimated or treated badly for being a woman in drag racing Even just watching from the stands is a visceral experience, with vibrations shaking your body and the ground.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Spectators are advised to wear ear defenders - the noise is comparable in decibels to standing next to a fighter jet taking off.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: The highest official speed ever reached in a Top Fuel drag race is over 346mph, compared to 231mph in a Formula 1 Grand Prix.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Brakes alone cannot slow the cars fast enough, so parachutes are deployed from the car's rear at the finish.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: The abrupt halt is "like someone kicking you in the chest", says Callin.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: "You lose your breath." Top Fuel drivers need lightning-fast reactions and the physical endurance to withstand the intense forces.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Precision driving skills are crucial as constant tiny adjustments are needed to keep the car on track.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: "It has to be instant reactions with everything," says Callin.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: "By the time you've thought about it, it's too late… You really have to be one with the car." And drivers need sheer guts.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: As Callin's rival and friend, 32-year-old Swiss driver Jndia Erbacher, jokingly tells the BBC - it takes "balls".
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Top Fuel cars surge from zero to 100mph in less than a second Callin clinched her second successive European Top Fuel title in September at the Santa Pod drag strip near Northampton.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: It is the fourth year in a row that a female driver has won the title.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Meanwhile in the US, the record-setting Brittany Force won the US championship - run by the National Hot Rod Association (NHRA) - in both 2017 and 2022.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Drag racing is "highly unusual" among motorsports, says Fran Longstaff, chief innovation officer at More Than Equal, which supports and campaigns for women in motorsports.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Seeing women competing and winning in the sport has become "normalised rather than treated as exceptional", she says, including with "sustained success" in Top Fuel.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Research she co-led into why drag racing leads the way for equality in motorsport did not identify physical or biological factors, she says.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Instead, she points to a "continuous stream of visible female role models", as well as the sport's "accessible grassroots structure, junior programmes, open pits and family-oriented, collaborative culture".
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Shirley Muldowney was the first woman to win the NHRA Top Fuel Championship In drag racing, points out Callin, women started winning major races "decades and decades ago".
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: The best known is Shirley Muldowney, dubbed the "first lady" of drag racing.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: The first woman to gain a Top Fuel licence, Muldowney won the NHRA championship in 1977 and went on to become the first driver to win three titles, with further wins in 1980 and 1982.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: She had to battle to be allowed to compete at high levels, and faced hostility at times from other competitors and fans, but is now lauded for her perseverance.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: When the BBC spent time with Callin in the pits between races at Santa Pod, surrounded by roaring engines and the smell of burning rubber, she signed autographs for fans - young and old, male and female - as her team prepared her car.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: "I never feel I've been underestimated or treated badly for being a woman - never," Callin says.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: This is in stark contrast to the experiences of women seeking to enter Formula 1.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Young female drivers have spoken about being deliberately pushed off karting tracks by male competitors, and facing sexist comments in person or online.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: More Than Equal's research also highlights a close-knit, family-oriented, collaborative culture in drag racing.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Like many top drag racers, Callin is from a racing family.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: She has been involved since childhood, following in the footsteps of her father and uncle, who both raced competitively.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Similarly, Erbacher's father Urs was a three-time European Top Fuel champion.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: And Brittany Force is the daughter of John Force, who holds 16 NHRA drag racing titles.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: The 300mph motorsport where women keep winning Watch the full documentary following Susanne Callin as she bids to retain her European Top Fuel title Female drivers have also shown that success is possible in Top Fuel in the years after having children.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Callin took a break for more than a decade to raise her daughter and stepdaughters.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: It was when she returned, aged 35, that her career really began to flourish.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Similarly, Finnish driver Anita Mäkelä has won the European championship four times – three of them after a six-year break focusing on her children and running her family's chicken farm.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: For Callin, racing is ingrained in family life.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Her dad is still part of her team.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Her husband, Keith Bartlett - sometimes referred to as the "godfather" of UK drag racing - runs Santa Pod Raceway.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Two of their daughters were driving junior dragsters at 80mph before they were old enough to sit a standard driving test.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: The youngest, Jacqueline, is now 19 and racing in adult classes.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: The culture is collaborative, despite fierce competition - evident at last year's championship, when Erbacher offered Callin spare parts after her car was damaged.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: "We hate each other at the starting line, but we love each other at the finish line," Erbacher says.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Erbacher jokes that it takes "balls" to compete in Top Fuel Asked about safety, both Callin and Erbacher talk about having "respect" for the car and the risks.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Over the years, strict procedures and regulations in Top Fuel have evolved to improve safety.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Drivers wear fire-resistant suits and sit in highly protected cockpits.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Even after dramatic accidents, drivers in many cases escape relatively unscathed.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: This includes Callin, who has had two major crashes, suffering a concussion and a bruised collar bone, but no lasting injuries.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: She says serious accidents are a "very small percentage".
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Even so, she is still not sure she would be comfortable if her daughter wanted to race in Top Fuel, with its extreme speeds.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Erbacher says her father initially refused to let her race, but relented when she declared she would do it with or without his help.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: More Than Equal also points out that the financial barriers to participating in drag racing are lower than for some other motorsports.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: It takes millions of pounds to reach Formula 1, requiring high levels of sponsorship.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Elite drag racing is also expensive, but not on the same scale.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: At the lowest levels, accessible racing events called "track days" take place, where participants can turn up and drive their own ordinary cars.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: In the biggest Top Fuel championships, drivers race for themselves and earn points based on how they perform against their competitors.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: The European championship consists of four events - two in the UK, and one each in Germany and Sweden - in which each driver takes part in six races.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Prize funds are limited, mostly serving as a contribution towards costs.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: The US championship is on a larger scale, with 20 events across the country.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: The NHRA has not published a breakdown of prize money, but according to drag racing website Competition Plus, there is $500,000 (£378,000) for the 2026 winner, and significant pots for winners of individual events throughout the season.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Indian driver Uvashri Kannadasan Balajeyanthi first raced in a modified Skoda Octavia The US, Europe and Australia have all seen female drag racing champions, but in other parts of the world, the sport is less well established, Top Fuel is rare and the picture is more varied.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Individual women are breaking barriers across a range of different motorsports, and in some countries female drivers are carving out space in drag racing.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Women have begun to make an impact in Brazil's popular drag racing scene, including Fabiola Dal Bo who has held a category record in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: A team in South Africa hosts all-female drag races, while the popular reality TV show The Fastest in Arabic has raised the profile of women racers in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: In India, 35-year-old Uvashri Kannadasan Balajeyanthi has clinched victories over male rivals in India's major drag racing series, Valley Run, with wins across three different categories in events from 2022 to 2024.
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Known as Octy Girl in reference to the modified Skoda Octavia she first raced in, she tells the BBC she has "mixed feelings" when her achievements are met with surprise: "Why do they have to get shocked?
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Anyone can drive, right?" But she adds "sometimes I feel proud… I'm breaking the barrier of being in a male-dominated sport".
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.text: Back in Europe, however, Callin says being a woman on the drag strip is "super-normal".
sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning

sentences.article_title: Faster than F1: The extreme motorsport where women keep winning
