sentences.text: Oxevision uses infrared sensors and cameras to monitor patients while they are in their bedrooms Ten mental health trusts have been reported to the health regulator after problems with patient consent procedures when monitoring patients using camera technology.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: The issue emerged during the latest hearings of the Lampard Inquiry, which is examining the deaths of more than 2,000 people who spent time in mental health units in Essex between 2000 and the end of 2023.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: The infrared technology is used in patients' bedrooms and can monitor breathing and pulse without staff having to enter the room.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: NHS England told the inquiry it had passed information to the Care Quality Commission (CQC) after reviewing the use of digital monitoring systems, including Oxevision.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: Gareth Harry from NHS England told the inquiry their oversight was not 'ineffective' Baroness Lampard has said she would introduce interim recommendations on the introduction of some technology if she believed there was a "risk to patient safety".
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: The inquiry heard NHS England first became aware of safety concerns linked to Oxevision in 2021.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: Giving evidence, Gareth Harry, NHS England's National Delivery Director for Mental Health, Learning Disability and Autism, said concerns had been raised about consent, patient observations and human rights.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: The inquiry was shown an internal NHS England email from 2022 in which one staff member said they had been aware of trusts where patients were "not being given the choice to refuse being filmed".
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: In 2023, NHS England wrote to mental health trusts saying monitoring technology should not be introduced as a blanket approach and decisions should be made for each patient individually.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: It said if possible, patients should be involved in those decisions.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: Harry said NHS England later reviewed practice after concerns were raised by campaign group Stop Oxevision , external .
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: The inquiry heard that review found 10 mental health trusts were "not operating their consent mechanisms in line with the digital principles".
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: The trusts that have been referred to the regulator have not been named.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: Harry said NHS England wrote to the CQC on 2 October and shared the findings with inspection teams.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: Bereaved families - pictured outside a previous evidence session - have been raising concerns about the monitoring technology What is the Lampard Inquiry and what could it change?
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: Lampard Inquiry: Five things we've learned so far Lawyers representing bereaved families questioned why it had taken several years for NHS England to act after concerns were first raised.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: Harry said day-to-day responsibility for following the guidance sat with individual trusts rather than NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: Counsel to the inquiry Teniola Onabanjo asked Harry if NHS England recognised that the enthusiasm for innovation might "outpace" the scrutiny of consent and ethics when it comes to camera technology.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: "I would expect every provider of mental health services to have their values and behaviours driven by a human rights approach to mental healthcare," Harry said.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: A CQC spokesperson told the BBC: "Providers have a responsibility to offer safe, high-quality care in line with relevant guidelines.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: "CQC considers all information of concern that is shared with us, and should a provider fall short we can and do take action." The regulator is due to give evidence to the Lampard Inquiry on 7 October.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: Giving evidence in October 2025, Laura Cozens, from LIO Health, the company behind Oxevision, said it was important the technology was properly explained to patients.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: She also said it had helped prevent serious incidents, including falls on a dementia ward.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: The current hearings are expected to continue until 15 October, with a further virtual hearing on 20 October.
sentences.article_title: Ten NHS trusts referred over monitoring consent

sentences.text: Baroness Lampard has said she could issue interim recommendations if urgent patient safety concerns are identified before the inquiry's final report, which is due in 2028.

sentences.text: Overcoming social anxiety can be tricky but experts have shared some tips to try and make it easier It was during her teenage years that Mary began to become anxious in social situations.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It got so bad she developed depression and had to have time off school.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: By the time she started university, she avoided group settings altogether.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I didn't join clubs and societies like others did," says Mary (not her real name).
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I just thought nobody would want to get to know me.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I didn't really make a single friend during my whole degree." Mary's social anxiety was so bad that she was diagnosed as having social anxiety disorder - something that affects up to 12% of people , external at some point in their lives.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: But plenty more report struggling more generally.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: As students return to uni, we asked experts how to overcome these feelings whether in your first, or final year.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: This video can not be played What makes you socially anxious?
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Research has suggested more than a fifth of university students face some kind of social anxiety during their studies – and it has been linked to lower grades, poorer relationships and isolation in a study by the universities of Chichester, Coventry and University College London , external .
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: For many, university marks the first time they have moved out of home – and the expectation is that they will quickly make friends.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Mary, who went to the University of Exeter, says she did try.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "When I first got there I went to one society, but everybody was talking to each other and I had a sudden fear come over me.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I felt I wouldn't fit in and I went home." Mary, who is now 25, describes her social anxiety as like an out of body experience.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: When she was talking to new people, heat would rise in her face and her hands would begin to tingle.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I'd almost feel myself separating from my body.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I forgot how to form words," she says.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "After social situations I was often left with the sense that I'd done something awful.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I had an all-consuming feel of shame.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I kept thinking there was something fundamentally flawed in me." Neil Greening, chair of the Social Anxiety Alliance UK, says this is a typical characteristic of people with social anxiety.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "People think they have a personality flaw.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: They internalise it rather than seeing it as a recognisable condition that they can get help for." The key thing to remember: It's fairly normal to feel a little shy or anxious when meeting new people, being in new situations or going for a job interview.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Social anxiety is when it actually stops people doing things, Greening says.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: For those with a clinical diagnosis it can have a debilitating impact like it did for Mary.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "It can be hard to admit to any form of social anxiety in a world where extrovertism and social confidence is generally admired.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Mary, who has moved on to do a postgraduate course, is now managing her social anxiety better.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: After her undergraduate degree she got support from the NHS in the form of a talking therapy called CBT.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It is considered the gold standard treatment for social anxiety and encourages people to re-frame their thoughts and change their behaviours.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Prof David Clark, a psychologist at the University of Oxford, says he would like to see more people come forward for therapy but says people can also take steps to help themselves.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: The first step, he says, is to stop obsessive self-focus .
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "People with social anxiety often monitor themselves constantly during social situations.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "Focus outwardly on the conversation, other person or your surroundings." He says you also need to test your fears with behavioural experiments by asking a question in a meeting or saying something in a group and noticing what happens.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "People with social anxiety often assume negative outcomes – that they will embarrass themselves or think others will find them boring.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Testing that can help people break that.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: It's frightening, but it can really help." He also says they need to drop safety behaviours , such as rehearsing every sentence, avoiding eye contact or sticking close to one particular person.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: And finally, Clark adds, try to avoid post-event rumination .
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "It's so easy to distort what actually happened." This is something Mary can empathise with.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I used to play things over constantly in my mind.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: What I've learnt is that dealing with social anxiety is a gradual process.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: The therapy really helped me, but so did something a friend said to me a couple of years ago.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "When I said I didn't want to join her in meeting some of her friends, citing my poor social skills, she said she'd never thought that about me and that I shouldn't undersell myself.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: I was overcome with emotion.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: "I'm now pushing myself to engage more.
sentences.article_title: Hidden habits that make your social anxiety worse - and how to break them

sentences.text: Baroness Lampard said that the inquiry was of "national interest" The chair of a public inquiry into mental health deaths said she would make interim recommendations if she identified issues that "might pose an urgent risk to patient safety".
sentences.article_title: Early Lampard findings could come within weeks

sentences.text: Baroness Kate Lampard is examining the deaths of more than 2,000 people who died while under the care of Essex mental health services between 2000 and the end of 2023.
sentences.article_title: Early Lampard findings could come within weeks

sentences.text: The Lampard Inquiry will hear further evidence during hearings beginning on 5 October before deciding whether recommendations were needed ahead of a final report, Baroness Lampard said.
sentences.article_title: Early Lampard findings could come within weeks

sentences.text: Any recommendations were expected to focus on inpatient safety, including resuscitation procedures and monitoring technology used to detect patients in distress.
sentences.article_title: Early Lampard findings could come within weeks

sentences.text: Oxevision uses infrared sensors and cameras to monitor patients while they are in their bedrooms "Those two matters are not specific to Essex and therefore the evidence the inquiry hears will be of relevance to service providers across the entire country," Baroness Lampard said.
sentences.article_title: Early Lampard findings could come within weeks

sentences.text: "It may carry implications for the care and treatment provided on all mental health units." One system under examination as part of the inquiry is Oxevision, which can take footage, record breathing and pulse rates and is used by a number of NHS mental health trusts in England.
sentences.article_title: Early Lampard findings could come within weeks

sentences.text: Concerns have been raised about privacy, dignity and whether the technology could be used as a substitute for face-to-face care.
sentences.article_title: Early Lampard findings could come within weeks

sentences.text: Tammy Smith, whose daughter Sophie Alderman died in 2022, previously told the inquiry: "It actually takes away human interaction.
sentences.article_title: Early Lampard findings could come within weeks

sentences.text: They are at their most vulnerable.
sentences.article_title: Early Lampard findings could come within weeks

sentences.text: "They need those conversations.
sentences.article_title: Early Lampard findings could come within weeks

sentences.text: They need someone to ask, 'Are you OK?
sentences.article_title: Early Lampard findings could come within weeks

sentences.text: Do you need anything?' We all need that." What is the Lampard Inquiry and what could it change?
sentences.article_title: Early Lampard findings could come within weeks

sentences.text: NHS England said any vision-based monitoring technology must support a human rights-based approach to care and be used in line with legal requirements and appropriate patient consent.
sentences.article_title: Early Lampard findings could come within weeks

sentences.text: The inquiry is due to hear evidence from NHS England, the Care Quality Commission and the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency during hearings between 5 and 15 October.
sentences.article_title: Early Lampard findings could come within weeks

sentences.article_title: Early Lampard findings could come within weeks

sentences.text: Sarah Mackay, known as @fitwsarah online, says her energy levels change through her cycle A woman points to a colour-coded grid dividing the menstrual cycle into four phases, each paired with a different list of exercises.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "When you're bleeding, you want to be doing steady-pace jogging, Pilates, barre, walking, resting," she tells viewers.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This is one of thousands of videos on TikTok and Instagram suggesting that people change their workouts depending on where they are in their menstrual cycles - something known as 'cycle-syncing'.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: So-called cycle-syncing workout plans have surged in popularity online, with Google searches for the term rising 740% since 2022 and more than 55,000 TikTok videos now using the #cyclesyncing hashtag.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Most of the advice is shared by fitness and wellness creators rather than medical or research experts.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Kelly McNulty, a researcher at Leeds Beckett University specialising in menstrual cycles and exercise, says there is evidence that some women experience changes in symptoms, energy or perceived strength across their cycle.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But that is different from evidence that all women should train in a particular way at a particular point, she tells the BBC, adding that these videos are "a trend based on marketing rather than any kind of research or evidence".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "There isn't any research to support that kind of phase-based prescription," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This video can not be played Should you sync your exercise routine with your period?
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: A key issue is that menstrual cycles are highly individual, McNulty adds - they can differ between women, and one woman's experience can also change from one cycle to the next.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: That makes the blanket advice often found on social media difficult to apply, she explains.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Many cycle-tracking apps and programmes are also designed around relatively regular menstrual cycles that are 21 to 35 days, which can make their recommendations less applicable to people with irregular periods, or those using hormonal contraception.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She doesn't follow a prescriptive plan, she says, but instead makes changes intuitively.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my luteal phase I'll try and ease off in the training," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my follicular phase, I'm so energised, I feel like I can lift so much heavier.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: I like to try and get my long runs in." Burgoyne also welcomes the growing attention on women's health, and says that exercise and nutrition research has historically focused heavily on male bodies, with findings then often applied to women.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Sarah says she has sometimes hit personal records while on her period Fitness creator Sarah Mackay, known as @liftwsarah on Instagram and TikTok, has also noticed her energy, motivation, cramps and mood change through the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But she deliberately avoids strict plans because, she says, "there are too many variables at play".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Some online plans advise women to avoid intense training during their period, she says, yet she has sometimes hit personal records while menstruating.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "The problem is not that the menstrual cycle is irrelevant," she says, but that "not everything is predictable".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Dr Faye Bate, a trained medical doctor and women's health expert, is also wary of advice suggesting all women should train differently according to their menstrual phase.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "A one-size-fits-all model of 'you should be exercising this way in this phase and a different way in a different phase' shouldn't be advice that applies to all women," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She is concerned that repeatedly telling women they are likely to be weaker or less capable at particular points in their cycle could create a "nocebo" effect - where negative expectations themselves influence how someone feels or performs.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty tells the BBC that routinely easing off resistance training could also limit progress.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Strength training is particularly important for women, who face a higher risk of osteoporosis later in life.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: While cycle-syncing itself may not be backed by strong evidence, the experts we spoke to did suggest being "cycle-aware".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty says tracking your cycle can be a useful way to understand your own patterns, while Dr Bate also encourages women to become more familiar with how they feel at different points in the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Both welcome the fact that menstrual health is being discussed more openly, but say the focus should be on individual experience, rather than rigid, phase-based rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In practice, that might mean having painkillers ready before your period, taking a rest day when symptoms are worse, or easing off a workout if you feel unusually fatigued.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: For Dr Bate, "the most important part is tuning in to how you feel".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In other words, use your cycle as information rather than a set of rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Mark and Roberta Harrison say Hobie was funny and mischievous The police watchdog has criticised a force after call handlers told a family raising mental health concerns to ring a locksmith.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: On 6 August 2025, Hobie Harrison's parents called Norfolk Police to request a welfare check after he failed to respond to them.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: He was found dead the next day.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said the force's 101 call handlers should have referred the family to mental health services, but instead suggested they contacted a locksmith.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Norfolk Police said it was reviewing the findings and it had been following the force's Right Care, Right Person (RCRP) policy , external , which limits officer attendance at welfare calls to cases involving "immediate risk to life".
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The IOPC said the call handlers should have asked more probing questions to assess Hobie's level of risk and there should have been a better explanation to his parents about why officers were not sent under its RCRP guidelines.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Hobie's parents, Mark and Roberta Harrison, made a second request for a welfare check for their son to Norfolk Police the following day.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Officers attended and found the 30-year-old dead in his flat in Norwich.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The couple say they were left unsure where to turn after being told their concerns for their son did not meet the threshold for a police response In October 2025, the family made a complaint to Norfolk Police over its handling of their call.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: In its report, the IOPC criticised Norfolk Police's response to that complaint after the force told the parents officers should not have attended either call, including the second one that led to Hobie's body being found.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The IOPC called that reply "unnecessary and insensitive".
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Hobie had previously threatened suicide and Mark said: "We'll never know whether he was still alive when we first called and whether something could have been done.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: David Ford, the watchdog's director of oversight and casework, said: "We have raised our concerns with the force around its interpretation of RCRP and monitoring of the initiative.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: "As a result... the force has said it will undertake a review to examine whether there are any organisational learnings." Norfolk Police said it could not comment further because an inquest has yet to take place, which is due to happen in November.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Hobie's parents say the 30-year-old loved music and enjoyed gardening Hobie had schizophrenia and developmental trauma and was under the care of the Norfolk and Suffolk Foundation Trust Community Mental Health Team.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: His parents said he had a history of drug use.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The couple adopted Hobie as a child and said he had been in "good spirits" the last time they saw him before his death.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: In August 2025, the family said they became concerned he had not spoken to them for more than 24 hours as he usually contacted them "several times a day".
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: "The non-contact was just... it didn't happen.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: So, it was very, very unusual," said Roberta.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The couple went to Hobie's flat but could not use their key to get inside because his key was still in the lock on the inside of the door.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: "We were 100% certain he was in there and he wasn't responding, so we knew there was something seriously wrong," said Mark.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: If you have been affected by any of the issues in this story, you can visit the BBC Action Line for support and information Unable to break in, they called Norfolk Police and told call handlers that their son had a history of self-harm and suicidal threats.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: After consulting a supervisor, the staff member told them the situation did not meet the threshold for a police response and suggested they consider contacting a locksmith.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: "We didn't know how to make a decision at that point or what to do quite frankly," said Roberta.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The following morning, after a second call to police, officers attended the flat and found Hobie's body.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: "If the police are no longer going to come, then it has to be very clear who's got the responsibility," Roberta added.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The Harrisons say regular calls, walks, shopping trips and meals together formed part of their daily routine with Hobie RCRP was first developed by Humberside Police in 2019 and has since been adopted by forces across England and Wales.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The policy is intended to reduce police involvement in welfare and mental health-related incidents so officers can focus on crime and immediate threats to life.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Norfolk Police said the approach, which it introduced in 2024, had reduced officer attendance at welfare-related incidents, from 11,831 in the year before the policy was introduced to 9,229 by its second year.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: The force said there was "no defined response" to welfare concerns and the appropriate pathway depended on the circumstances.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: His family say Hobie enjoyed riding his bike when he felt well enough to get out and about The Norfolk and Suffolk Integrated Care Board said support could involve health, social care, ambulance or police services.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: A 2024 national agreement on the policy , external said people experiencing mental health crises should not be left without support.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Some coroners have raised concerns about RCRP.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: A Prevention of Future Deaths  report into the death of Sophie Cotton in County Durham , external said the policy appeared to overlook that mental health teams could not enter locked premises.
sentences.article_title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears

sentences.text: Andy Burnham has set out his plan to transform Britain, including by ending the existing state pension triple lock from 2030 to help fund a new national care service.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: In his first Labour Party conference speech as prime minister, Burnham also said he wants to pave the way for greater public control over housing, water and energy services, and potentially reform the UK's electoral system.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: After days of questions over how to fund his social care reforms in England, Burnham pointed to changing the triple lock to generate "significant savings".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: His plans would see the state pension increase every year at least by inflation or 2.5% - but remove the automatic annual link with average earnings.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Andy Burnham: Northern PM's long journey to power In front of a packed hall and watched on by family and friends, Burnham spoke for more than an hour - at times pausing and appearing to hold back tears as he referred to his father, Roy, who died earlier this month .
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Arriving on stage to the sound of "All Together Now" by Liverpool band The Farm, Burnham made the song title a theme of his speech.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He said he wanted to "draw a line on a decade of division" and to "stop doomscrolling on posts running Britain down".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Burnham also told conference that he wants to "put the country on a new path" and recalled his family's "working-class aspiration" and how the government wanted to "unlock" this for others.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: There was an expectation that Burnham's time in Liverpool for his party's conference would see him flesh out his vision for the future of the country.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: In the conference hall, he offered more details albeit with some of the proposals relating to the content of the Labour manifesto at the next general election rather than delivering immediate action.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Burnham's plan to offer free at the point of use social care in England is among those being developed so it can be put before voters in 2029.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He said it would be "fully funded and not through borrowing".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Explaining his long-held ambition to make changes, he raised his family's experiences - including how his grandmother Kitty's engagement ring was "ripped from her finger and stolen in a care home".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He argued a national care service was a "landmark" policy that would be "as significant as the creation of the NHS itself and utterly essential to securing its future".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Before turning to the pension triple lock changes, Burnham accepted he may "pay a political price" by trying to make the reforms but argued "someone has to go through the pain barrier and rip the plaster off".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: The triple lock was introduced in 2010 by the coalition government and designed to ensure the value of the state pension was not overtaken by the increase in the cost of living or the incomes of working people.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: It means the state pension rates rise every April by either inflation, earnings growth or 2.5% - whichever is the highest.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Burnham said this will stay in place until 2030, at which point he would like to "adjust it".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He said: "The state pension will continue to rise every year at least by prices or 2.5%.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: And it will hold its value relative to earnings over time so that pensioners will always share in the rising prosperity of the nation.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: "But this change will generate significant savings which we will use to build up our national care service.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: "Some may not realise it but older people with nothing more than the state pension, or only a little more, can find themselves paying care charges today from that small income.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Under my plan, this will no longer happen." Officials have suggested the change could save £15bn a year by 2040.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Jonathan Cribb, deputy director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said savings "are likely to be relatively small in the first few years, but rise substantially over time".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: He also said "we should not expect this reform to save enough that it could fund universal social care in the next parliament".
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: The political backlash was immediate.
sentences.article_title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care

sentences.text: Have you ever slept next to a snoring partner and woken up feeling stressed, unfocused or forgetful the next day?
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: As snoring is relatively common, it is often left untreated and dismissed as a harmless irritation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But according to experts, sleeping next to a snorer could be impacting your health.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Snoring is caused by the vibration of the soft tissues in our upper airways during sleep, explains Dr Clare Simon, a dentist with a special interest in dental sleep medicine.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: About 40% of the UK adult population snores, with the issue affecting more men than women, says the British Snoring and Sleep Apnoea Association (BSSAA).
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: And 75% of people with a snoring partner say they have had their sleep impacted, according to a US survey by the Sleep Foundation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know about the impact on partners - and what you can do about it.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Prof Ama Johal, a consultant orthodontist and sleep expert at Aerox Health, explains that the partner of a snorer can become "so impacted upon that it's almost a last-ditch effort on their part to get up and go sleep in a separate room because they have to sleep".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: He adds: "As humans we physically can't function without that necessity." Prof Ama Johal says many couples put up with the negative effects snoring for too long During the night, we cycle through different stages of sleep in repeating patterns, usually every 90 minutes.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: The deeper stages of this cycle are important for physical restoration.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If sleep is frequently disrupted, you may spend less time in the restorative stages, meaning you can wake up feeling tired, even if you've spent a lot of time in bed, the BSSAA explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Your brain processes and stores information from the day during sleep.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Fragmented sleep - which can happen if you're waking up due to a snoring partner - can interrupt this process, impacting your focus and memory.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Disrupted sleep can also impact hormone regulation, which affects your energy levels and motivation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Sleep also plays a role in regulating the brain systems involved in stress and emotional response.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: When it is disrupted, these systems can become less balanced, which may make you feel more irritable and less able to cope with stress.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: This is something Meg Warren, 29, experienced when her former partner's snoring would keep her up.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says: "Without fail, after a snoring-induced wake up I would feel on incredibly high alert." Meg, a charity media officer, would prod him throughout the night and try to coax him from his back to his side.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says she would wake up "feeling groggy and dazed, sometimes so much so that it would feel like a hangover".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Meg Warren felt 'groggy and dazed' after a night of little sleep due to her former partner's snoring Anna-Louise Dearden, a 52-year-old journalist, says she sometimes sleeps in a separate room from her partner due to his snoring.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Having this option allows her to prioritise getting enough rest when the snoring is particularly bad.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: There are things that can be done, say both Simon and Johal.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But first, it is important to distinguish whether your partner is simply snoring, or whether they have sleep apnoea.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: "What you don't want to do is simply make someone quieter at night while potentially missing an underlying sleep-related breathing disorder," Simon says.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Signs of sleep apnoea, a disorder that causes a person's breathing to repeatedly stop and start during sleep, include pauses in breathing, choking at night, waking frequently, and suffering from morning headaches.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If this is what you are dealing with, you could be recommended a Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) machine, or even surgical treatment in some cases, Simon explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: For simple snoring, Simon said that lifestyle changes can make a difference, such as losing weight, stopping smoking, reducing alcohol intake before bed, or changing your sleeping position - such as laying on your side rather than your back.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: You can also suggest to your partner that they see a GP, who will be able to advise further or refer you to a specialist.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: An expert might suggest treating nasal obstruction or allergies, if this is what is causing snoring, or wearing a custom mouthguard to gently push the lower jaw forward and keep the airway open.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Johal says too many couples put up with snoring "for too long", which impacts their relationships and wellbeing.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: "The key thing is that there is help out there, it's just tapping into it." How sleep tracking can make your sleep worse The hidden cost of the night shift and how to sleep it off

sentences.text: Sleep scores, magnesium, white noise machines - what was once the simple act of sleeping has become a minefield.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Trying to optimise sleep in this way is called "sleepmaxxing".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Take it too far, and you could end up with "orthosomnia" - the clinical term for an obsession with achieving perfect sleep.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: While it's not formally recognised as a condition in the UK, doctors tell the BBC they've noticed signs of orthosomnia in their patients, with some bringing their sleep tracker data into appointments convinced, wrongly, that they have a sleep disorder.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: That fixation is actually making people's sleep worse, they warn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: So how and why did sleep become so complicated?
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: And if sleepmaxxing isn't the answer, what is the elusive secret to a good night's sleep?
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The first commercial fitness tracker to incorporate sleep analysis was the Fitbit Classic in 2009.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Since then, many others - including Garmin, Whoop and Apple - have integrated sleep trackers into wrist-worn devices, as have smart rings such as Oura, Ultrahuman and RingConn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: These devices vary, but in general they all provide users with a report of their night, broken down by sleep stages - time awake, light sleep, deep sleep, and REM (rapid eye movement).
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Many also give users a "sleep score".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: But the concept of a sleep score is "completely made up", according to Dr Alanna Hare, consultant of sleep medicine at the Royal Brompton Hospital in London.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "There's nothing recognised in sleep science that is a 'sleep score'," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "That's just been created by manufacturers." This video can not be played How sleep-tracking can make your sleep worse Hare says she's noticed trackers causing anxiety among her patients.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I've noticed more patients coming to me with data from various trackers, with lots of questions about sleep that... is probably contributing to their sleep difficulties," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Even though some have had medical tests with reassuring results, this hasn't allayed their fears, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "It's great that there's more focus on sleep as part of wellness," she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "But sleep just does not respond well to attempts to perfect it." One proposed lawsuit against Oura, filed last month in San Francisco, alleges that Oura rings are unable to accurately measure sleep quality and sleep stages, and instead rely on AI-generated estimates that have "a coin flip's chance of being correct".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: In response, Oura told the BBC that it "stand[s] behind our science, research and accuracy claims".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "We're committed to clearly communicating what Oura measures, what it estimates, and how members should use that information," the company added.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Studies also show sleep trackers can affect how you function during the day, even if they're not accurate.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: In one study , external from the University of Oxford, participants were given sleep trackers which assigned them a sleep score.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The scores were randomised, however, and had no relation to how the participants had actually slept.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The next day participants rated their mood, fatigue levels and alertness, before tests checking their focus and reaction times.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Researchers found that the people told they'd slept badly reported feeling more fatigued, and were less mentally alert - even though the sleep scores were all fake.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: This is something Jess Hill says she noticed in herself after getting a Garmin watch several years ago.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I started to rely on the watch as my Bible for whether I slept well or not," the 32-year-old HR professional from London tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I would think, 'I've had awful sleep so I'm going to really struggle today', even if I actually probably had okay sleep.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I was awake the other week for four hours in the night, and my watch was like 'wow, great sleep!' - I literally was awake from 01:00 until 05:00," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The BBC has approached Garmin for comment.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Jess's sleep scores weren't matching how she actually felt Dr Neil Stanley, sleep expert and author of the book How to Sleep Well, argues that gamifying sleep is creating more disordered sleeping.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "The thing with tracking your sleep is that it gives you a number, and this means you have a target," he tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "So you get into this cycle of worrying about your quality of sleep or the quantity of sleep based on figures." He says he carried out research into actigraphy - wrist-worn sleep trackers - around 40 years ago.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Though commercial trackers now are a bit more sophisticated, they work in much the same way - by measuring your movement - and have the same limitations, he says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "If you want to measure sleep, you have to measure the brain," Stanley adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "Unless you're measuring the brain's activities, you're not measuring sleep." Keeping your bedroom cool, dark and quiet - within reason.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "That doesn't mean it needs to be pitch black, exactly 16C or totally silent," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "It should be coolish, darkish and quietish." Seeing bright light in the morning, which is good for regulating your circadian rhythm - that is, your body's natural clock.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Doing light exercise, and eating a "healthy, Mediterranean-style diet with plenty of plant variability".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Above all, keeping it simple - "anything else, you don't need it".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Sally Williams told the BBC how isolated she became during the "run-up" to menopause For three years, Sally Williams struggled to understand what was happening to her as her mental health deteriorated and her life fell apart, spending almost 11 months in hospital across eight admissions.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: She left her finance job, was separated from her teenage son and found herself fighting for her life, unaware her symptoms could be linked to perimenopause.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: "No one joined the dots," Williams said.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: I joined the dots and it was transformational to start hormone replacement therapy and literally come back to life." Williams, who initially self-diagnosed, wants other women to be aware of perimenopause, the years leading up to menopause, which she described as the "danger zone".
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: Perimenopause , external , which commonly begins around the age of 46, is when women experience menopause symptoms while still having periods.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: Symptoms can include anxiety, mood swings, brain fog, hot flushes and irregular periods, with some women taking hormone replacement therapy (HRT) to help  alleviate the symptoms.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: What is the menopause and what are the main signs?
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: How does Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) work?
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: When her symptoms began in her late 40s, Williams, from the Wychavon area, said doctors she saw initially thought she had depression.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: "I had multiple attempts on my life, two significant ones, one where I was in a wheelchair for three months for polytrauma, and this was in Covid, so there were no visitors.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: I had no contact with anyone," she explained.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: This was at perimenopause time.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: My message to women is that, menopause is not the danger zone, it's the run up, it's the 45 to 54." For Williams, who said she was "unrecognisable" before her eventual diagnosis, it was HRT which eventually helped her, but she said it may not be for everyone.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: The drug , which isn't suitable for some women, tops up and stabilises oestrogen levels, sometimes in combination with a synthetic or bioidentical version of progesterone.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: Williams is set to speak about her hard fought menopause diagnosis at Meno Fest at Worcester Rugby Club on 7 October , external , as part of Menopause Awareness Month.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: The free event is being held with the aim of helping people to gain greater understanding of how perimenopause and menopause can affect every aspect of life from physical and mental health to relationships, work and family life.

sentences.text: Williams told the BBC of how isolated she became during the "run-up" to menopause.

sentences.text: I didn't see my friends, my family for three years and I was a recluse.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: And my son, who was in his teens, I probably saw him three times," she explained.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: "He had leave his school and his friends and he had to go and live with his dad because he couldn't see me.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: I couldn't care for him." It was also important that men recognised what was happening to women during perimenopause, she added.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: "I think men need to come into the conversation as well, and I'm not just talking husbands and partners, I'm talking sons," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: "It was devastating and there's relationships that have been broken that will never be put back together.
sentences.article_title: 'Perimenopause cost me my job and family life'

sentences.text: I'm very sad about that." If you have been affected by the issues in this story, help and support is available via the BBC Action Line .

sentences.text: The chief statistician said the survey provided a "vital insight" into the lives of young people A survey for young people on topics including health, wellbeing, school life and social media is set to open in October.

sentences.text: Statistics Jersey said the survey would be offered to students from Year 4 to Year 12 and would run from 5 to 16 October.
sentences.article_title: Survey to show 'vital insight' of children's lives

sentences.text: It said the 2026 Children and Young People's Survey was voluntary, anonymous and could be completed online.
sentences.article_title: Survey to show 'vital insight' of children's lives

sentences.text: Officials said it would be the first time the survey would ask participants about social media apps and generative AI tools, including how often they use them.
sentences.article_title: Survey to show 'vital insight' of children's lives

sentences.text: Chief statistician Ian Cope said it provided a "vital insight" into the lives of children and young people on the island.
sentences.article_title: Survey to show 'vital insight' of children's lives

sentences.text: Statistics Jersey said it would explore whether young people had caring responsibilities and enough food for each day.
sentences.article_title: Survey to show 'vital insight' of children's lives

sentences.text: It said the results would be used across the Government of Jersey to inform policy and improve services.
sentences.article_title: Survey to show 'vital insight' of children's lives

sentences.text: "We have worked directly with students this year to help shape the content, ensuring it reflects the issues that matter most to them," Cope added.
sentences.article_title: Survey to show 'vital insight' of children's lives

sentences.text: "New questions on social media, generative AI, caring responsibilities and food security will help build a more complete picture of the opportunities and challenges facing young people today." sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Around 10,000 people in the Kent region will have already received jabs, as part of the response to the March outbreak.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young people aged 18-25 starting university or moving into residential further education settings for the first time in autumn 2026 are also eligible.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: In Wales, those aged 17-18 will receive a letter invite, while those aged 18-25 who are entering higher education will need to contact their health board later in July.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis can be caused by many different types of viruses or bacteria, which are spread through close contact with a person who has them.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England
