sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: All three companies have appeared in court this week, arguing they should not need to provide so much information in response to Ofcom's formal requests.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta has separately also argued Ofcom should not be able to levy fines for breaches based on its global annual revenue.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: It also contends that its messaging and image-sharing apps should not have to face additional requirements under the OSA, such as tackling paid-for fraud ads.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: People shouldn't be punished for working harder, Badenoch says Kemi Badenoch has said a Conservative government would scrap the "cliff edge" that means parents in England lose out on childcare support when they earn more than £100,000 a year.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch unveils plan to end £100,000 childcare 'cliff edge' ahead of Tory conference

sentences.text: The announcement comes as Conservative members gather for the party's annual conference in Birmingham.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch unveils plan to end £100,000 childcare 'cliff edge' ahead of Tory conference

sentences.text: Badenoch, who arrived in the city on Saturday, has vowed the party was new and different from the one that lost the 2024 general election.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch unveils plan to end £100,000 childcare 'cliff edge' ahead of Tory conference

sentences.text: The Conservatives - who have been polling behind Labour and Reform UK over the past year - are expected to use the four-day event to lay out more of their policy agenda ahead of the next general election.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch unveils plan to end £100,000 childcare 'cliff edge' ahead of Tory conference

sentences.text: Ahead of the conference, the Conservatives produced a 100-page essay setting out their principles , external including a "central" belief that business, rather than governments, create growth.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch unveils plan to end £100,000 childcare 'cliff edge' ahead of Tory conference

sentences.text: It argues that governments should create the conditions for growth, particularly through the tax system.
sentences.article_title: Badenoch unveils plan to end £100,000 childcare 'cliff edge' ahead of Tory conference

sentences.text: She said the policy, under which state pensions rise each year by the highest of inflation, average wages, or 2.5%, was "the right policy for pensioners".

sentences.text: The party said its childcare announcement would be a "first step" in broader efforts to address issues in the tax system which damage incentives to work or invest.

sentences.text: A woman convinced her former partner she had given birth to two children who most likely did not exist in what a High Court judge described as an "extraordinary" and "elaborate campaign of deceit".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The man, who has not been named but was referred to as John in the judgement, applied to the Family Court after he was told the woman had sold their two children for a combined £500.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The case heard that the man received messages and photos of the children and paid the woman around £30,000 over the course of two years.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: But in a hearing in February, the woman, who was referred to as Jane, told the judge she had lied about the pregnancies for revenge, claiming the man had abused her.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The court heard the man believed he was the children's' father because in late 2022 his partner told him she was pregnant, sent pictures of an ultrasound image and had become "visibly pregnant" as time went on.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In May 2023, shortly before the first baby was due, the woman called the police alleging she had been assaulted by the man.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: He was arrested and subsequently held on remand for several months, Mrs Justice Judd said in her ruling which was published on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Following this, the woman sent a message to his stepfather saying the baby had been born as well as sharing baby photos.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: At one stage she is said to have sent voice notes to her former partner's mother in the middle of the night with the sound of a baby crying in the background.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Later, she told the man she was pregnant again and the baby was due in August 2024.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: However, before the due date, the couple split up and did not reconcile.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman would go on to tell the man's mother the baby had been born.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman admitted to the court she had told him she was pregnant when they were together, and afterwards, but conceded she had told a series of elaborate lies and that there were, in fact, no children.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She argued she was menopausal at the time and could not have been pregnant and bank statements show she attended a tanning shop on the day she said she had given birth, Mrs Justice Judd said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In her judgement, the judge concluded that the "factors that weigh against the children genuinely existing were very strong, stronger than the factors pointing the other way".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She said the man was the victim of a "sustained and elaborate campaign of deceit" which also impacted his mother and closest friend.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: "Added to this, the behaviour was cruel, leading a man and his mother to believe they had children and grandchildren respectively.", the Judge said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The judge added she was unable to conclude the woman's motive for her behaviour but said financial fraud was a "possibility"  and that the "complex mental health problems" she suffered from may have also played a part.

sentences.text: Experts recommend that those who may be more vulnerable - such as older people and babies and young children - should take extra precautions.

sentences.text: As the body gets hotter, blood vessels open up.

sentences.text: This lowers your blood pressure and makes your heart work harder to push the blood around the body.

sentences.text: This process can cause mild symptoms such as an itchy heat rash or swollen feet.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: At the same time, sweating leads to the loss of fluids and salt and, crucially, the balance between them in the body changes.

sentences.text: Rosanna Brown was advised to end her pregnancy because her baby had a life-threatening medical condition A woman whose baby was too ill to be born is calling for better awareness of choosing a termination for medical reasons.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: Rosanna Brown, who lives near Waterlooville, Hampshire, was advised to end her pregnancy with son William in 2023 because he had a rare and life-threatening medical condition called Chaos syndrome.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: Continuing the pregnancy would have risked both their lives, but Rosanna said the experience was made even more difficult due to a lack of training around medically-advised abortions.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: An NHS spokesperson said it offered "comprehensive support for women whose unborn baby is diagnosed with a serious health condition".
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: Rosanna said she understood why so many people who suffered a termination for medical reasons (TFMR) just told others they had had a miscarriage.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: "Because it's a type of abortion, you have the pro-life pro-choice argument, you are thrown into the middle of that," she said.
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: "You have this feeling that your grief isn't as valid because you've chosen [it].
sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: Jane Fisher from the Arc charity said it was important to break the taboo around TFMR Rosanna is campaigning for change, including for the term TFMR to be properly used, which she said it was not on her son's forms.

sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.article_title: Baby termination was 'our most loving choice'

sentences.text: Around one in four children started school in England and Wales last year not fully toilet-trained, and teachers said they have been spending over an hour a day changing nappies, according to the latest research from the children's charity Kindred Squared , external .
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Felicity Gillespie, chief executive of Kindred Squared, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that children not being potty trained when starting school was "a real concern for teachers".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "They tell us that they're losing, on average across the country, a day a week of teaching time to dealing with potty-training issues." Gillespie is keen to spread the message that "it's best for children to be coming out of nappies" when they are between 18 and 30 months old.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "When the teacher's leaving the class to change someone's nappy, the rest of the class is having their learning broken up.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: So everybody loses out,” she added.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The ability to listen to and follow instructions is another skill that helps pupils get the most out of learning when they start reception class Jo Mould, who teaches reception at Robert Wilkinson Primary Academy in York, said she has noticed an improvement in pupils being ready for school this year.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "We've spent more time teaching in these last three weeks than we have in previous years," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "The children have come in so ready to learn, because they're more settled and regulated socially and emotionally.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: We've had a really, really positive start to the school year." Jo Mould says not having to deal with toilet training has meant more time spent teaching her pupils York councillor Bob Webb said the impact of the scheme had been "so positive" for both schools and families.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: But he acknowledged a potential "gap in support" for parents between seeing health visitors with their toddler, and the child later arriving at school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: He said the key to the scheme's success was collaboration across health visitors, schools and other community settings, but that there was "always more that could be done at an earlier age".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Twenty local authorities across England have now committed to adopt York's model, developed by Kindred Squared, and use it to encourage earlier potty-training in their areas.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: That means they were assessed by teachers on being able to complete tasks like going to the toilet and paying attention in class.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The government has said it is still committed to increasing that proportion to 75% by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Early Education Minister Paul Waugh said it was "encouraging to see this pilot helping more children develop the confidence and independence they need before starting school", stressing the importance of parents taking early steps towards toilet training.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: In York, Mould said she hopes next year's parents will take on potty-training even earlier.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "Ideally we'd be at the point where [children] don't need that support when they get here, because they've already been trained by the time they get to us." Do you have any views, comments or questions about this story?

sentences.text: Children should be introduced to the world of work at the start of primary school, says the author of a major report into youth activity in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Former minister Alan Milburn says children as young as four should be learning about different careers, with work experience placements made mandatory for 14- to 16-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: However, teaching unions warn of the "significant pressure" already facing primary schools and say practical considerations must ensure all schools have access to the support.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The latest data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) suggests 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 in the UK were not in education, employment or training (known as Neet), between April and June 2026.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn told the BBC "in primary school, it's really about opening their eyes and giving them a sense about what is possible".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Despite a push towards apprenticeships and work experience in Years 10 and 11, for many the journey towards becoming Neet starts well before their 16th birthday.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: As a result, Milburn says children should be introduced to the world of work much earlier in their school journey, with dedicated space in the curriculum to "broaden horizons".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The final instalment of Alan Milburn's review into Neets is due to be published this autumn He told the BBC this could be achieved by employers giving talks in primary schools and offering taster sessions to children.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "It'd be good if employers came into schools and said, 'Look, this is what's going on, these are things that are possible.'" Milburn says that for Key Stage 4 pupils - aged between 14 and 16 - experience must be given in a real workplace with employer feedback.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Work experience needs to be mandatory.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: It makes a big difference," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Milburn also emphasised the difficulty some young people face when trying to find work experience placements.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "There are about four in ten people aged 14-16 who aren't getting any work experience at all," he said.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Education is devolved in the UK, so while Milburn's review looks at the picture in all four nations, his recommendations regarding education are specific to England.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Currently in England, careers guidance must be offered to students aged 11-18 and work experience is not statutory.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The government has said its vision , external is to "guarantee two weeks' worth of work experience for every young person" in England.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: In both Scotland and Wales, career-based learning is already a requirement in schools for students as young as three.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Emma, from Kirklees, has grandchildren in Years 1, 2 and 4 and thinks primary school is too young to be introducing careers talks.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "In primary school, there is too much trying to get little kids to grow up too quickly," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Just let them be little kids.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: I know they have to learn and the world's changing, but still, give them a chance to be kids." But Zoe, another parent, disagrees.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "I think it's a good idea," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Paul Whiteman, general secretary of school leaders' union National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT), warns of the "significant pressure" already facing primary schools.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Whenever new mandatory requirements are proposed, it is important to be clear about what might have to give way to make room for them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Whiteman also highlights the value of existing programmes such as "Primary Futures", which bring in volunteers from different professions into schools to "challenge stereotypes and raise aspirations".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "The earlier young people can begin to make connections between what they learn in school and the possibilities that lie ahead, the better," Whiteman says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL), says having someone come into the classroom can really "enlighten [children's] motivation... and give them that sense of passion for all the opportunities beyond the classroom".
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Although he acknowledges that finding opportunities in rural areas could be more challenging.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Cases of antisemitism affecting university students and staff in the UK increased in the last academic year, according to a charity that monitors antisemitic incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The Community Security Trust (CST) said it had recorded 95 "university-related" incidents in the 2025-26 academic year - up from 83 the year before.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said the number had fallen from its peak in the year after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023 and the war in Gaza began, but remains "substantially higher" than before that point.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Universities UK (UUK) represents more than 140 institutions and said its members needed to "protect Jewish students and staff", adding that the findings were a "serious concern".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Lucy Powell, education secretary in England, said the findings in the CST report were "deeply troubling".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: "We expect universities to take a zero-tolerance approach to antisemitism, and are providing training to help university staff identify and respond to incidents swiftly," she said.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The CST defines an antisemitic incident as "university-related" if it concerns a student, member of staff or academic at a UK university "in their academic or student capacity" - including on campus and online.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: In 2022-23, the last academic year before the 7 October attack, the CST recorded 53 incidents.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: That grew to 272 in 2023-24.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: A report from the charity examining the past two academic years says reported incidents fell in 2024-25 and but grew again in 2025-26.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The most common type of incident recorded by CST over both years was abusive behaviour, including verbal abuse, comments made in person or online and antisemitic graffiti.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Its report said that, for the first time, there were two occurrences of extreme violence in 2024-25.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: It said there were six reported assaults across both years, eight incidents of damage and desecration to Jewish property - five of which were in student accommodation - and ten threats.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Around two-thirds of reported incidents involved antisemitic language or targeting alongside references to Israel, Gaza, Hamas, the 7 October attack, and the subsequent conflicts in the Middle East.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: The war in Gaza was triggered by the Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostage.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Israel launched a mass military offensive on Gaza in response which has killed around 74,000 people, according to the Hamas-run health ministry.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: He added that universities had "a duty to ensure that Jewish students and staff can study, work and participate on campus the same as anyone else".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Raphi Leon, president of the Union of Jewish Students, said the report "must be a shot in the arm to boost action to support Jewish students and tackle antisemitism".
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Vivienne Stern, chief executive of UUK, said: "The rise in antisemitic incidents in the UK, including on university campuses, is a serious concern.
sentences.article_title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns

sentences.text: Dr Chris McCarthy says the pillow that's best for you depends on the way you sleep (branding has been obscured) "I am one of those people," says Dr Chris McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "I do take my pillow with me." You may have seen those people at the airport - a pillow stuffed under an arm as they drag their suitcases to check-in.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Or you might be one yourself - attached to a pillow that's soft enough to settle into but robust enough that it's not bunched into a ball by morning.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy insists he's not being fussy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He's a top physiotherapist and knows the wrong pillow can be a pain in the neck.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He doesn't take his abroad, but as soon as he gets to his hotel he starts "faffing about" with the pillows - and he's got a tried and tested trick to make even the most lacklustre one fit for sleep.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Here's his guide to choosing the perfect pillow for you.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: What makes the perfect pillow?
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: One advertised for your sleeping position?
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Sliced Bread separates science fact from the marketing fiction.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy, an associate professor at the Manchester School of Physiotherapy, says the right pillow will depend on what position you sleep in.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He tells the BBC's Sliced Bread podcast that most people fall into one of three categories of sleeper: side, back or front.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy discourages front sleeping as your neck is turned one way for a long period of time.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "Inevitably a muscle or ligament gets stretched and a bit irritated," he says.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "If there's one thing there's a really good consensus on... in the physiotherapy world about treating spinal pain, it's don't sleep on your front." When choosing a pillow, back sleepers should consider the flexion at the top of their spine, a curving that increases naturally in many people as they age.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: If you have a bigger bend "it means you need a slightly thicker pillow than someone who's got a very flat back," says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: For side sleepers the key measurement is the width of your shoulders.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: In general, the broader you are the thicker the pillow you will need.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: But you also need to consider your mattress.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: McCarthy says how much you sink into your mattress "makes a huge difference in the subsequent height you then need from the pillow".
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "Broad shoulders need a thick pillow [if] you're on a very firm mattress," he explains.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "If you're on a softer mattress, then you need a thinner pillow because your shoulder sinks into the mattress [more]." This is less of an issue for back sleepers as they don't sink into the mattress as much as side sleepers do.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: If your pillow feels too flat, McCarthy suggests placing a folded towel underneath and changing the number of folds to adjust the height.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Then you can make a rough measurement to help you pick a new one.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Specialist pillows are often advertised as contoured, ergonomic or orthopaedic - but McCarthy says their effectiveness isn't completely proven.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "There is a little bit of fairly scrappy evidence to suggest that having a little bit of a higher front of the pillow, which goes into the neck area... does help [side sleepers]." To see if a higher front helps you sleep better, you can try McCarthy's towel trick by rolling it and placing it underneath your pillow.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: He urges side sleepers to pick a position that keeps their back straight.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: For back sleepers, some manufacturers advertise a pillow with a dip in the middle that is raised at the sides.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: It does put people into a good sleeping position, says McCarthy, but some of his patients have found them "a bit claustrophobic".
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Someone who has a large and heavy head also needs a thicker and firmer pillow, he adds.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Feather and down can keep you cool on warm nights because they wick away heat from your head, says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: But they can change shape during the night, particularly if the sleeper moves around a lot and the pillow can end up bunched towards the headboard.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: "What starts off as a nice, flat, supported surface becomes a wedge and so your neck is then kinked up." Hollow fibre and microfibre fillings can hold shape better though they generally don't wick away heat as well, says McCarthy.
sentences.article_title: How to find your perfect pillow - according to an expert

sentences.text: Some are made with a firmer material in the lower half of the pillow, which help retain the shape during the night.

sentences.text: Dr Amara Naseem says GPs are under pressure to offer more appointments, rather than a focus on quality treatment Pressure to provide more GP appointments is making it harder to include checks for gynaecological cancers within the 10-minute slots, doctors have said.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Dr Amara Naseem says her clinics always overrun as it takes about 20 minutes to sensitively take a detailed history and carry out internal examinations.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: A reduced number of practices in her area means she has taken on more patients and fears there is a risk that women will not raise gynaecological symptoms or attend screenings if appointments are rushed, painful or not handled well.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: The Welsh government said it was increasing investment in primary care and recruiting up to 100 extra GPs.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Research by cancer charity Tenovus, in support of Claire's Campaign , external , found about half of the 100 GPs surveyed across Wales felt limited consultation time was a major concern.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: A third also had concerns about "over-referring" people for further testing to rule out cancers, given hospitals are already overstretched.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Currently, 95% of patients put on the suspected cancer pathway are later told they do not have cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: But doctors said teasing out the cancer cases at an early stage could be challenging when symptoms such as bloating are hard to distinguish from benign conditions including irritable bowel syndrome.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Naseem said the pressure from the Welsh government was to "offer more appointments to the patient, rather than about the quality of the treatment".
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Lowri Griffiths of Tenovus said incidence and mortality rates for gynaecological cancers in Wales were higher than the UK average - something she added the Welsh government needed "to get to grips with".
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Pledges to increase GP numbers were promising, she said, "but unless we address both the primary care setting and the hospital setting, the system won't work".
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Lowri Griffiths says Wales needs to be "more aspirational" in gynaecological care Naseem said many women's health issues may require an internal examination, which requires time to be done "in an empathetic and sensitive way".
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: She added: "I'm working in a very diverse community, also in a deprived community, where uptake of screening is already low." She said in communities where myths existed around screening, time is also required to explain what is involved and allay fears and potentially work with interpreters.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Dr Kathrin Thomas said her friend Claire O'Shea was "a real feminist" Dr Kathrin Thomas, a former GP and public health specialist, got involved in Claire's Campaign when her friend Claire O'Shea was given a late diagnosis for a gynaecological cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Claire, from Cardiff, died last year, aged 42.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Thomas said GP numbers in Wales had "almost flat-lined" while the workload had increased, especially in more disadvantaged areas where there were "fewer doctors, fewer nurses and the healthcare needs are much greater".
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: She is also involved with Deep End Cymru - a network of GP practices in the most deprived areas.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: "We've got a big difference in the cancer experience in more deprived communities - cervical cancer in particular," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: "There's a wide inequity between women in more affluent areas and women in poorer areas." Of the 1,200 women diagnosed, about 470 patients die from a gynaecological cancer, either of the womb (uterine), ovary, cervix, vulva or vagina, in Wales each year.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Screening is only available for cervical cancer and it does not detect other cancers.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: "Cancer outcomes are improving dramatically over the decades, but we're struggling in Wales to get the outcomes that other richer countries are getting," said Thomas.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: The waiting times for gynaecological cancer treatment in Wales have improved significantly over the past year, from 34% of patients being treated within 62 days, to 51.3%.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: However, the most recent Wales average for all cancers was 60.1% against a target of 75%.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Maria Bailey has been fundraising to make more "grab and go" bags for other patients treated for cervical cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Thomas said continuity of care came up repeatedly among the Tenovus survey of GPs.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: "You have a 20% less chance of dying if you have the same team that looks after you," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: Maria Bailey feels being able to see the same GP was a factor in her own cervical cancer diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: 'Cancer checks harder' to do in 10-minute appointments with GP

sentences.text: WhatsApp is introducing new parental controls for teenagers, as tech companies continue to come under pressure to provide more age-appropriate experiences for children.

sentences.text: The social messaging app's new tools will give parents a range of options, such as being told when their child joins or leaves a group.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: It will also let them decide on privacy settings for their account.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: In a blog post, WhatsApp, clarified parents would not be given the power to see the messages their teen is sending and receiving, which along with calls would stay private and protected by end-to-end encryption.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: And it said the controls were optional, which social media analyst Matt Navarra called an "obvious weakness".
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: He said the move was "fairly convenient" for Meta, which owns WhatsApp, because it reduced the company's reliance on age verification by putting some responsibility on parents and teenagers.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "Meta is trying to show regulators we have a child safety system, we have parental controls and we're rolling it out across our platforms," he said.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: "I think the big unanswered question is whether enough families will actually use it." The minimum age to use WhatsApp is 13 in the UK, although it is higher in some countries.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: According to the firm, parents will be able to adjust or switch off the controls at any time.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.text: Some of the new privacy tools include selecting who can see a child's profile photo and who can add them to groups.
sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: WhatsApp introduces optional parental controls for teenagers

sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.article_title: Schools not ready for AI and 'crying out' for government guidance, report warns

sentences.text: "Put simply, education has not kept pace with how – and how much – young people are already using AI, and that gap is starting to show up as a loss of perceived value in the institution itself," the report says.

sentences.text: When parenting advice becomes too much Before Rosie Whitfield became a mum, she imagined herself parenting very calm children.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Then I had two wild boys," she says with a laugh.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Following the birth of her kids, Rosie spent hours online looking for the best advice and was drawn to one particular approach to parenting: Gentle parenting, which focuses on empathy and mutual respect with little emphasis on punishment, albeit with boundaries.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: But she constantly worried her choices, from sleep schedules to handling toddler tantrums, were "ruining their lives forever".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Rosie believes her confidence and intuition were stripped away as she questioned every parenting decision.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Government research suggests that around two-thirds of parents with young children feel overwhelmed by the amount of parenting information available and struggle with conflicting advice, with many turning to social media for support.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Rosie Whitfield says she felt overwhelmed by the amount of parenting advice online when looking for guidance on raising her two sons.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: And it's not just the early years.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Research from the charity Action for Children found that many parents of teenagers who initially contacted the charity for help with school avoidance, ADHD or mental health, often went on to describe their own anxiety, exhaustion and uncertainty of how to parent with empathy and patience when close to burnout.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Faced with an array of parenting philosophies, or "brands" to choose from, is all of this advice helping parents or making them more anxious?
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: And is there really a best way to parent?
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Or, as we strive to become the perfect parent, are we losing our intuition?
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Parents today are confronted by parenting styles including "helicopter parenting", which is focused on closely monitoring and protecting children from harm, and "tiger parenting", which involves strict parenting and high expectations for achievement.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: There are also "snowplough parents", who try to remove obstacles from their child's path, and "dolphin parents", who aim to be firm but flexible.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Author Matilda Gosling, who wrote Evidence‑Based Parenting, says many of the parenting fads or trends complicate what should be a straightforward relationship between a parent and child.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Throughout history, you get these swings from one extreme to the other," she says.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Gentle parenting is seen by some as the latest swing away from a strict, detached parenting style popular in the 1990s, which often relied on controlled crying, the naughty step and time out.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: It is built around understanding, empathy and respect but also emphasises the importance of boundaries.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: One of the most widely studied models of parenting comes from developmental psychologist Diana Baumrind.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Baumrind identified three parenting styles, later expanded to four: authoritative (high warmth and high control), authoritarian (low warmth and high control), permissive (high warmth and low control), and neglectful (low warmth and low control).
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "Authoritative is the gold standard," says Gosling who has looked at more than 1,000 studies.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Research has found that children raised with an authoritative approach, combining warmth with clear boundaries, tend to achieve better academic results, have higher self-esteem and stronger social skills.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: But where gentle parenting fits within that framework is disputed.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Gosling believes that it falls on the permissive side.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "It's very much child-led.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: The child ends up having so much control that there's no sense of safety coming from the outside." However, Sarah Ockwell-Smith, who is widely credited with coining and popularising the term 'gentle parenting', strongly disagrees.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "It [gentle parenting] is not remotely permissive," she says, putting it firmly in Baumrind's authoritative category.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Clear boundaries are "super important".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Social media, however, is flooded with memes of exhausted parents calmly negotiating with a child having a supermarket meltdown, something Ockwell-Smith finds deeply frustrating.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "I have to step away from the Instagram reels and the TikToks because I just want to comment, 'This is not gentle parenting'".
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: "You have house rules, family limits, discipline and consequences.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: But the difference is we look at discipline as learning and teaching rather than punishing." Toddler tantrums and teenage behaviour, she argues, should be viewed through a lens of ongoing brain development, not 'they're being naughty' or 'they hate me'.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: But despite the term being popular, Ockwell-Smith believes that gentle parenting is still a fringe movement and that authoritarian parenting remains the dominant style.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: Around 80 years ago, American paediatrician Dr Benjamin Spock published a book called Baby and Child Care, which went on to sell millions of copies and became the main source of advice for mothers for generations.
sentences.article_title: When parenting advice becomes too much

sentences.text: The opening line was "Trust yourself.

sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: Kagan and Japan's Kenso Soai for providing a solution to the chemical mystery of life's asymmetry.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: The researchers discovered how nature exclusively makes the correct version of a molecule - rather than its mirror image.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: For example, amino acid molecules, the building blocks of proteins, exist as two forms that are each other's mirror image.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: But living organisms on Earth only function with one of those forms.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: The Nobel laureates answered the question: why does life favour just one of these mirror image molecules over the other.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: In organic chemistry, this property is known as "chirality", so chiral molecules have both right and left-handed forms.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: You can think of them as looking like our hands - not identical, but each a mirror image of the other.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: And while nature almost exclusively produces the version it requires to function, chemical reactions in a lab usually create a 50-50 mix of both left- and right-handed molecules.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: When it comes to making drugs, this is particularly significant, because each version behaves differently when it interacts with our bodies.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: So, one might have disease-fighting properties, while the other version does nothing or even causes harm.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: The development of the Thalidomide drug is an example of this.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: In the 1950s it was prescribed to pregnant women suffering with morning sickness.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: But it is a chiral molecule - the right-handed version is an effective treatment, but the left-hand is toxic.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: The original drug given was a mixture of the two, and it was later discovered that the body will convert between the two.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: The result was thousands of children, born to women who took the drug, developed severe disabilities.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: Heiner Linke, chair of the Nobel Committee for Chemistry, explained: "Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai have provided a solution to a chemical mystery that is over a century old: how homochirality - the selective production of the correct version of a molecule - can emerge spontaneously.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: "The chemical reactions they have developed are spectacular." Henri Kagan, who is at Université Paris-Sud, first discovered a new way of manipulating chemical reactions in 1986.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: This allowed him to create a greater excess of one of the mirror images than had previously been thought possible.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.text: Kenso Soai from Tokyo University of Science took the next step in 1995.
sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.article_title: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry

sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: One study found that the birds are forced to move higher in the mountains as their natural habitat in the alpine meadows above the tree line get crowded.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: The other says the monal is changing its pitch to cut through human noise in a busy valley.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: "These two studies give a useful warning for other more vulnerable species - if the monal is forced to change both its voice and its address, how are the more sensitive species responding?" says Vishal Singh, an environmental practitioner working on ecology and climate issues in the Himalayas.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: Dr Rajeev Lochan, lead researcher of both studies, told the BBC that they chose to study the monal as the bird has a narrow habitat range - it moves seasonally between the lower montane zone - an ecological belt found on the lower slopes of the mountains - and high-elevation alpine zones.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: This, he says, makes it a key indicator of ecosystem health in the north-western Himalayas.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: "If the species is facing issues on this particular landscape, there might be a chance that the ecological disturbances are affecting other birds too," said Lochan.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: Found high in the Himalayas, the monal lives in alpine meadows above the forests The monal, researchers say, can be seen as a stand-in for the health of a fragile Himalayan ecosystem pushed to a tipping point due to unregulated tourism and heavy urbanisation.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: While the region has always drawn tourists, trekkers and researchers given its scenic landscape and biodiversity, rapid infrastructure expansion in the past decade has made more places accessible, increasing footfall and disrupting the wildlife.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: This, coupled with mounting human pressures, suggests that climate change is emerging as another major threat to the region's already vulnerable biodiversity.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: "There are a lot of factors at play but at a broader level, the problem is that the economic development of the region is not aligned to its ecological integrity," Singh said.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: Currently, the birds are found in alpine meadows, located high in the mountains above the forests, which form some of the Himalayas' most important seasonal grazing and biodiversity-rich habitats.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: The researchers modelled how climate change could shift the monal's suitable habitat across the Indian Himalayan region in the states of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: It was based on the kind of global climate models and emissions scenarios used for assessments by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the UN's climate science unit.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: "These birds are now slowly moving upwards in the Himalayas as the snow is melting and vegetation is growing, making the area accessible to them.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: They are anyway being pushed upwards as their natural habitats in alpine meadows are being encroached upon by humans," Lochan said.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: The model assumes that the bird needs the current climate set-up that exists in alpine meadows in the future too, a reasonable but not certain assumption.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: The birds' seasonal migration may become increasingly difficult as changes in climate may force them to move to higher elevations on hills, to smaller and fragmented areas.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: Their population would be scattered in disconnected pockets, which reduces chances of breeding between groups and increases their risks of long-term decline or local extinction, which is already a threat, the study says.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: A male Himalayan monal displays its iridescent plumage during a courtship ritual aimed at attracting a female The second study, also conducted by Lochan, Dinesh Kumar Sharma and Anand Kumar, who work at the Hemvati Nandan Bahuguna Garhwal University, focuses on the bird's behavioural changes.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: They conducted the study in two valleys in Kedarnath Musk Deer Sanctuary in Uttarakhand - at Chopta, a tourist spot with busy traffic and visitors, and the largely quiet Madmaheshwar.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: They recorded more than 700 monal calls across both sites using microphones and passive recording devices and then measured pitch, call length and background noise levels for a year from April 2023.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: Birds in noisy environments consistently produced calls with significantly higher peak frequencies compared with those in quieter habitats, the study said.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: The researchers found subtle changes in the monal's pitch that could be picked up by recording devices but might go unnoticed by the human ear.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: "This does not mean that the species has undergone a permanent or evolutionary change in its vocal frequency; rather, our findings suggest behavioural flexibility in response to different acoustic environments," Lochan said.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: Compared with the birds in Madmaheshwar valley, the monal in Chopta also produced shorter call durations likely to cut through low-frequency human noise from traffic and tourist footfall.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: Bird calls are one of the most sophisticated forms of sound-based communication in the natural world, and significant changes can interfere with, among other things, their mating success.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: "When a species must raise its pitch to be heard over tourist traffic, or climb higher as meadows turn crowded, it reveals how human pressure is rewriting the rules of life in the Himalaya," says Anjal Prakash, a public policy professor at FLAME University and contributor to IPCC reports.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: Lochan says he and his team consider this a preliminary study and hope to expand the scope and depth of it.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: The research comes with the caveat that it is not conclusive on ecological consequences, and more research is needed.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows

sentences.text: But together, the two studies signal broader ecological stress across the Himalayas.
sentences.article_title: A beautiful Himalayan bird is changing its voice due to human activity, research shows
